utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind you, Mr. Kuehnel, of the affirmation which you made which still applies. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, yesterday we left off where I was just asking you to explain the steps that would be taken if a member of the Ministry of Interior was accused of an act of misconduct.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true. I received the following information the normal procedure would be in four steps. As soon as a member of the Ministry of Interior commits an infraction, his superior would write a report, and this report, I have copies of such reports, I have seen copies of such reports, the title of such a report would be a request for firing, or disciplinary infraction, and the report would be sent to the disciplinary commission and as soon as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I hope you can hear me. I apologise, Your Honour, and I'm grateful to the registry for the assistance. I can now be heard. Your Honour, simply we would like to make a similar objection than yesterday. We believe we are now going into the territory of what is in practice expert evidence about the structure and functioning of the disciplinary commission or disciplinary commissions, as Mr. Kuehnel indicated, and we believe that this evidence, Your Honour, had to be put through a witness capable of giving that evidence. We understand that hearsay evidence is admissible. We also understand that the scope of evidence that is permitted to be drawn from an investigator is limited in nature and also that evidence capable of enlightening the Chamber in relation to that matter was available to the Prosecution and could have been drawn out from existing witnesses. Your Honour, we indicated yesterday that unfortunately Mr. Galevski had passed away and we would like to reiterate once more that the Defence is put in a position where the witness is authorised to give evidence in relation to matter for which he has no expertise for which the basis of his knowledge has not been established and we believe that this evidence, as was indicated, we believe, in the Milosevic decision of September of 2002 should not come through a witness that is an investigator in this case, so we object to that sort of evidence being sought from Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Without troubling you, Ms. Issa, the submission is essentially that which was put yesterday and has been determined. The Chamber is not impressed the idea that this is evidence requiring expertise of a level and capacity which is beyond that presently available. The Chamber does recognise, as I'm sure Ms. Issa does, that there are limits to the reliability and weight which can be attached to evidence of this nature, based, as it is, upon what has been collected from others. And that is a matter which will, in some circumstances, have the capacity to affect whether the Chamber is able to be persuaded by evidence of this nature. But that aside, the evidentiary procedure being followed is one which in accordance with yesterday's ruling may continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If you can just pick up, Mr. Kuehnel, where you left off. I believe prior to the objection, you were indicating that normally what -- what occurs at the start of the -- the initiation of a disciplinary proceeding for an act of misconduct is that the superior of a member -- an MOI members writes a report relating the misconduct. If you could just pick up from that, please.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, the first step is that the superior of the person in question writes a report and sends it to the disciplinary board with a request for firing, as a violation of discipline. The second step is that the disciplinary board receives the report and makes a decision as to whether a hearing it is to be held. This hearing is recorded as part of the record as a discussion. A typical discussion in written form begins with mentioning the name of the people on the board and the name of the accused, and then the infraction is also mentioned. And the discussion, as far as I could see in the documents that I saw, is a process in which the accused is -- questions are put to the accused in the presence of his lawyer and then witnesses are heard, and the end of the discussion is -- well, the discussion ends with the signature of those present, of the head of the board and the members. And, at the end, the commission makes -- takes a decision as to whether to continue proceedings or whether the accusation can be done away with. The next step would be that the commission --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can stop you there for a moment before you get to the next step. Just to clarify, you mentioned the term "discussion." Can you briefly explain what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: A discussion in this written form means a hearing of the accused, during which members of the Ministry of Interior have an opportunity to express their views on the issue and proof is brought, or evidence is brought forth and witnesses are brought forth who give their views. Too.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. And were you advised whether or not the minister has a right to initiate this type of proceeding?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I might add here that this procedure in four steps was explained to me, and we had one, I was shown one example of it, and I asked Ms. Naumova who had the right to initiate such proceedings and asked her if the minister had the right to initiate proceedings, and the answer was yes, of course the minister has such a right to initiate proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. So moving on then --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I see that Mr. Mettraux is on his feet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Simply to clarify one matter and to object to one. The first clarification, if my colleague would be good enough to clarify with Mr. Kuehnel that the entire section that he has just explained was in fact told to him by Ms. Naumova. He has specifically mentioned Ms. Naumova in relation to the last aspect and we would grateful for this. Also, Your Honour, we would like to object to the answer given by Mr. Kuehnel in relation to information which he says he received from Ms. Naumova. We believe that on an issue such as this one, the witness herself should have been called if indeed that is the information she provided to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, do you wish to pursue any of those matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, that I believe the witness has said several times that he received this information from Ms. Naumova and in my submission it's clear on the record. But if Your Honour wishes me to pursue it once again, I shall do so. I don't believe that it is unclear. Mr. Mettraux can certainly cross-examine on it. As to the latter matter, I simply reiterate my earlier submission, in that it falls within the same type of information that Mr. Kuehnel has been testifying about up until this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber has understood the evidence of the witness so far to be based upon what was told him by the woman identified and not to be based upon his own independent knowledge, so on that basis, if you are content with that, Ms. Issa, you have no need to pursue the question with the witness further and that will be the basis upon which it is understood and received by the Chamber for the purposes of Mr. Mettraux's concerns. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, Mr. Kuehnel, can you please now explain the second step in this process as it was explained to you by Ms. Naumova.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] I think I just explained the first step. Now I would go to the third step.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, the third step, I apologise, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The third step, begins once the commission has decided that the disciplinary proceedings would continue, and in this step, a proposal is made for sanctions, and this proposal would then be sent to the minister of the interior. And in the fourth step, a decision is then taken about it. It is perhaps necessary at this juncture to mention that in the documents I saw and as to what I heard, according to what I heard, I learned that the third step, the writing of the proposal, takes place at the same time virtually as the decision. In practical terms the disciplinary proceeding makes its -- takes its decision at the same time as the rest, and everything is sent to the minister at the same time. I was told, and I saw this in the documents, that often the minister's decision different than the proposal sent to him, so this means that the minister can either accept the decision, the proposal, or he can change it. I was also told that the commission only has two possibilities for sanctions: One being to fire the employee; and the other being a financial sanction.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sorry, could you please continue.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm. A reduction of the employee in his level of employment is not foreseen. The fine involves a percentage reduction in his salary for a certain time. In the documents that I saw and from what I learned, I saw that in many cases the decision of the minister as to a fine was different from the fine proposed; either the period of the fine was changed or the percentage of the reduction in salary was changed by the minister. I also saw cases in which the minister acquitted cases. Everything I'm telling you here was explained to me and I was shown examples, a concrete example, from the files while I was there during my work.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was able to note the veracity of all this myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to very briefly, Mr. Kuehnel, deal with how the records of the disciplinary committee are archived. Can you briefly explain where these records for a disciplinary commission are normally stored?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was told about this too; this was something I learned when I was there. In general, the files are archived according to persons, according to individuals, and not according to disciplinary infractions. What I mean is that an infraction and the documents for it are in a file containing the name of the person in question -- or filed under the name of the person in question, and this file is archived in the organisational department where the person in question works.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Should I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, if you have more?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] As a practical example of this, I can say when a member of the police in Skopje commits an infraction, then it is Skopje which is responsible. One exception of this is that if a member of the Ministry of Interior dies or leaves the ministry, then his file is archived at the central police services. The organisation of the archiving is in the sector for common affairs, which is part of the centralised police service.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. Kuehnel, you mentioned that you reviewed all the cases that were listed in 2001 and 2002. Can you explain how you carried out that search?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm. I began -- I can't find the German word that I'm trying to use. I read the cases, looked them through on the basis of the two lists for 2001 and 2002 which contained all the cases,, these lists gave me the names of information on the accused, on their names, information as to which organisation they worked for, the type of infractions they committed, and the sanctions imposed upon them. On the basis of this material, I was able to make a preliminary selection, on the basis of certain filter criteria, which I can explain, with relation to the geographical structure and the events in Ljuboten, I limited myself to investigating the files of the centralised police service, the SVR Skopje with the -- including the units in question, such as the tactical units, PSOLO DKP, and also saw the files of the Ministry of Interior, and as far as I was able, the intelligence service UBK. The time-frame involved was from the time of the events, August 2001 until June 2002. Independent of this time-period, this time-frame, I also investigated certain individual cases before that period and after that period to have -- get an objective view of such disciplinary proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is, more or less, the search parameter that I applied. I then received the files in question. They were brought to me. They were not all in the same -- they were not all kept in the same archive, and I was able to go through the files in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you received the files in question, did you always get a full copy of the files that you requested?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to the copying of the acts, of the files, I always made a copy of each file to the extent that this was possible and -- economically possible. For August 2001 until June 2002, I limited myself to the proposals of the commission to the minister and the decisions of the minister. That is to say, to getting copies of these from the -- of this material from the files. I also, in order to understand how such files were constructed in these four steps, I also got copies of several complete files, either for this reason or for other reasons which arose at the time. So in conclusion, I tried primarily to investigate the proposals of the commission, to get copies of the proposals and to get a few files, a few complete files too.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can then please turn to tab 15 in the binder, 65 ter number 1072.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, please. I don't have the binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps if I can ask the assistance of Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you see -- if you look on your screen, Mr. Kuehnel --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: -- I believe that exhibit is now on the screen, and the Macedonian original is on the left-hand side. Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I recognise this document. It's right. It's one of the case studies, case files that I looked at and one of the case files that I photocopied. I had the complete file photocopied, and for the reasons already stated, there was another reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the reasons of fairness --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm going to interrupt you for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we may need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kuehnel, just to draw your attention. This is a file related to a Blagoja Dimitrovski. And if I can ask that we go to page 5, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. This is dated August 21st, 2002. And you see it's a decision in regards to Blagoja Dimitrovski and if I can just draw attention to paragraph 2, under the heading decision where it states: "His employment is terminated in the form of a dismissal, which dismissal I have exchanged with a pay fine in the amount of 10 percent of his monthly wage in the duration of one month." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting. I would just like to make one correction on the record. The previous document should be admitted as Exhibit P526. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. If we can then go to page 6, please. And just scroll to the very bottom. We see in the Macedonian version there's the signature, Ljube Boskoski, and the original seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Is this the type of a change in the punishment or the mode of punishment that you have seen from your review of these files, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's one possible example of a possibility to deviate from a decision - Sorry, I correct myself - to deviate from a proposal that was made.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I would seek to tender this document at this stage, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P527, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Turning, then, to tab 17, 65 ter 1064. And I just note for the record, Your Honours, that there is only selected portions that have been copied in the hard copy binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: This is in relation to an individual named Milan Mitrevski who was a police officer at the police station Gjorgi Petrov in Karpos. If we can please go to page 2. Do you see that at the top it's -- it say it is a decision to Milan Mitrevski, police officer in police station Gjorgi Petrov in DOR Karpos in SOR Skopje at the Ministry of Interior due to the violation of work discipline. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the second paragraph of that decision, if I can draw your attention to that, says that the employment is ceased with a termination, which termination is replaced with a pecuniary fine in the amount of 15 per cent for a duration of six months. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And starting at the very bottom of that page, if I can draw your attention to the paragraph or part of the paragraph that begins with the words: "Around 2200 hours." If I can just ask Madam Registrar to scroll down. It says: "Around 2200 hours Milan deviated from the order for performing service and headed to a restaurant 4 Aces in Volkovo where he stayed until 2300 hours, consuming alcohol, after which he continued according to the order from 0100 hours. At 0100 hours the named employee again deviated from the order and together with the military police conscript VPO (police reservist Zoran Trajkovski) headed to Sasa Stefanovski's place in Volkovo where they consumed alcohol. Whereupon the VPO Zoran took a hammer and a metal rod and around 0245 hours they damaged an object of the company El Greco in Kumanovo at which Zoran committed a criminal act, being attempted hard robbery, whereupon Milan stopped him finishing the act, which he covered up by not reporting it." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please turn to page 17 in that document. The ERN should be N006-5638. Thank you. Do you see at the top in the left-hand corner there's a reference to the sector of interior for the town of Skopje, department of interior, Cair?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And this is a document titled criminal charges against Zoran Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: For a criminal act, attempt of a serious robbery pursuant to Article 236 and in relation to Article 19 of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Macedonia which is in the middle of the page?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I could please ask Madam Registrar to turn to page 20 which is at N006-5641, ERN number.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the witness and counsel to pause between the question and answer for us to finish our work and for the transcript to follow accurately.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Just that paragraph at the -- the sole paragraph in that page which states: "Out of the above-stated and the attached acts apparently the reported Trajkovski, Zoran and Mitrevski, Milan committed a criminal act, serious robbery in an attempt that is set and punishable under Article 236 in relation to Article 19 of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Macedonia and therefore we would like to suggest to you to submit a request to the investigation judge for enforcement of a procedure in the aim to prove the criminal act and criminal liability." And it is signed by Ljube Krstevski, the head of the OVR Cair. Do you see that, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I can -- I would like to seek to tender that document at this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object to having this written document received in evidence by the Court. First I object to the relevance of the document, to the veracity of the data in it and the reliability of the data in it. Anyone person can file criminal charges or submit a criminal report. It is then another issue whether the prosecutor will process it and then develop a proposal to run a criminal procedure from it. Then the judge needs to issue a decision for a criminal procedure to be instigated and only after the criminal procedure is completed, the prosecutor decides whether to file an indictment on the basis of that procedure and evidence. And at the end it is the court that will bring a verdict based on this report, and according to the Criminal Code of Macedonia any person can lodge a criminal report and the prosecutor's office has not submitted any evidence as to the outcome of this criminal report. Perhaps an acquittal has been the result of this criminal report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, as to the issue of relevance, in this particular case the issue is not what the end result is with respect to the individuals named in this -- in this report. The issue that is relevant, in my respectful submission, is the very fact that criminal charges were referred to -- to the investigating judge in the first place, and that speaks to the issue of the third element under Article 7(3), which is a live issue in this case, as to whether or not reasonable and necessary measures were -- were taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document will be received. For clarification, Mr. Apostolski, it is not received as proof of the contents or the allegations that are recorded in it, but as a record of the procedure that was followed on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be received as Exhibit P528, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to 65 ter 1065, which is at tab 18 in the binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's the correct page, actually. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you see, Mr. Kuehnel, this is a decision dated August 29, 2001 where it states a decision that Zlatko Pejovski at the workplace police officer in the police station Rasce in the OVR Karpos in the SVR for the city of Skopje at the MOI of the RM is not responsible for the damage caused to the MOI and which consists of the loss of an official automatic rifle which the factory number 736959 and one magazine with 30 bullets. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then if we can please go to page 3 in the same document. Thank you. That's the correct page.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: This is a -- also a decision by the minister of the interior, and it refers to a Peco Kokarovski and if we look at the fourth line in that first paragraph underneath the heading decision, it refers to a violation of the work discipline which was done contrary to the rules and regulations of the ministry in relation to the work intentionally or with extreme negligence caused major damage to the ministry conducting their working --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you for slowing down.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I apologise. And it continues on with the last paragraph underneath the heading decision that says the employment is ceased with termination, which termination is replaced with a pecuniary fine and that is for Peco Kokarovski in the amount of 15 per cent of a monthly salary for the duration of six months and for Zlatko Pejovski in the amount of 10 percent of a monthly salary for the duration of two months. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Have you seen -- Mr. Kuehnel, have you seen this type of scenario before in your review of the disciplinary files where two persons are charged with a violation and one is found not responsible and the other has been found responsible?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen such cases from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I would seek to tender that document, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we won't object to the admission of the document. We would simply indicate that the file and case in question predates the time-frame when Mr. Boskoski became the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P529, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can please turn to tab 19 of the binder, 65 ter exhibit 1068. And if look at that first page, the cover page refers to a Peco Josevski. And if I can please ask Madam Registrar to move to page 2, please. I'm sorry, but in -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I just wanted to draw your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to the date of this decision, which is September 4, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the decision in the first paragraph indicates that it relates to Peco Josevski, as a workplace police officer due to the violation of work discipline with unjustified absence from work for three consecutive workdays, according to the Article 133, paragraph 1, item 3, of the collective agreement of the MOI. The employment is ceased with termination without a time-limit for a termination starting from the 17th of August, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just to draw your attention to the second paragraph underneath the heading elaboration. And that states: "Acting upon the proposal it has been confirmed that the named employee in the period from March 1st, 2001 until May 31, 2001, used unpaid leave from work from June 1st, 2001, until June 30th, 2001, used annual leave from 2000, and from the 1st of July, 2001, until 13 August, 2001, used annual leave from 2001, and he should have reported for duty," and it continues. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, have you seen other cases where an employee was terminated for unjustified leave in your review of the files?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've seen such cases quite often, in particular for 2001. And I noticed - and I think this is important to note this here - that such cases derive from a decision in the files.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, and if we can scroll down to the second page of -- of that document. And we see the Ministry of Interior seal with the signature of Ljube Boskoski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender that document at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P530, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can please then go to tab 20 in the binders, 65 ter 411.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, this is a document that is dated 19 November 2001, addressed to the government of the Republic of Macedonia and it's an opinion and proposal that is submitted in reference to the act that is submitted to "your act number 24-95/4 from 12 November 2001." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can please go to page 3. Now see that document is signed by Ljube Boskoski, minister for internal affairs. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can please go to page 2. Actually, I'm sorry, if we can please go back to page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: In the very first paragraph, right above the word "opinion," it states: "With reference to your act in which you press for a reply for case number 24-95/1 from 8 March 2001, we would like to inform you that concerning the submitted draft resolution on condemning the events and use of force by members of the ministry of internal affairs and to promote and accomplish the guaranteed fundamental freedoms and rights of citizens of the Republic of Macedonia, proposed by the group of members of parliament of the PDP, Party for Democratic Prosperity, in March 2001, the ministry submitted to the government the following ..." And if I could ask that we turn to page 2 now, please. And if I can ask Madam Registrar to focus on the last three paragraphs of the document. In the -- in the paragraph 3 of this document it states the following: "The analyses and statistical data of the Ministry of Internal Affairs indicate that when carrying out their responsible official tasks with a purpose to achieve state and public security, individual members of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the police, during carrying out extremely hard and complex tasks, when most often their physical integrity and life are at stake, in distinct cases they overstep their official authorisation and as a consequence of this, there are specific violations of freedoms and rights of the suspects, against whom official activities are being undertaken." And then it continues with -- about the middle of the paragraph that begins with when the relevant authorities of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. It states: "When this concerns the use of means for enforcement and firearms, such cases are being investigated by the department for internal control at the Ministry of Internal Affairs and in case it is concluded that there is indeed such an overstepping, disciplinary and legal measures shall be undertaken against these persons who have overstepped their official authorisation without exemptions." And if I can draw your attention to paragraph -- the last paragraph. It says: "As a result of the activities of the department for internal control of the Ministry of Internal Affairs in the period of time from 1998 to March 2001, all together 12 proceedings were initiated for breach of working discipline against 19 members of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, who, when carrying out their work tasks used physical force contrary to the rules and provisions of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, from the total number of employees from -- three of them were dismissed from work, ten of them were fined, and two proceedings initiated against authorised officials this year are still ongoing." Do you see that, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can please turn to page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can draw your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to the paragraph beginning with the words having in mind. "Having in mind the statistical indicators, the conclusion is that individual cases of overstepping the legal authorisation by authorised officials of the Ministry of Internal Affairs in the form of sanctioned exceptions in the work of the members of the Ministry of Internal Affairs are obviously incomparable and not disturbing in number with regard to the more and more evident, striking increase in the number of attacks upon the life of police officers of the ministry under conditions of carrying out the most complex tasks with armed terrorist attacks on the territory of the republic." And then it continues and it says: "For the aforementioned reasons, we propose to the government of the Republic of Macedonia not to support the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia to adopt the draft resolution by the PDP party group of Members of Parliament because there are no substantial grounds and concrete reasons for this, considering the insignificant small number of cases of overstepping authority by members of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the police while carrying out their tasks ... " Do you see that, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, do you know where this document came from?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We received this as an answer to a request for assistance that we sent, from the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I would like to seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have a series of objection in relation to the tendering of this document. The first is that in our submissions, Your Honour, the document is not in itself relevant, has no bearing on the charges. It doesn't refer to the events of Ljuboten in any way. But also as with other documents, Your Honour, and in particular documents which mention or relate to Mr. Boskoski, the accused, we do believe and do submit, Your Honour, that to the extent that these documents are said to have some relevance to the acts, conduct, or otherwise of the accused, these documents should have been tested with witnesses capable of giving evidence about the context, the circumstances and the nature of these documents. Mr. Kuehnel has been read the document and he has confirmed that he could indeed see what was in the text, as anyone else in the courtroom. Unfortunately, Mr. Kuehnel is not in a position to provide information as to the circumstances, the context or otherwise in which this document has been prepared, whether it has led to anything, whether there was any discussion at the government level about this matter, what the end result of this matter was. In other words, Your Honour, we would be unable or incapable of cross-examining Mr. Kuehnel in relation to issues other than the fact that Mr. Kuehnel might have received this document or might have seen it as part of its investigation. We would therefore, in our submission, be prejudiced if this document was tendered in this matter. We therefore submit that the document should not be admitted pursuant to Rule 89 (D) and Rule 95.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you just assist us a little more Mr. Mettraux. How do you see prejudice in respect of a document which, on its face, is a document of your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we believe that one matter which would be highly relevant to give any meaning to the document would be to ask in what circumstances the documents was prepared, who, if anyone, advised our client in relation to this matter, whether there was any discussion at the government level, whether the parliament followed the -- I'm sorry, the government followed the advice, whether there was any further discussion, whether the position of Mr. Boskoski changed at any stage the basis on which Mr. Boskoski took this position, the material perhaps on which he took the view that is indicated in this document. All these factors and others, in our submission, Your Honour, would be relevant to Your Honour's ability to give this document any weight or to regard it any way as a relevant document to the charges. In the absence of context, Your Honour, we believe that this document would be prejudicial to our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, first of all, this document is obviously relevant, because it's an indication of Mr. Boskoski's oversight over disciplinary proceedings and it therefore speaks to both his effective control over disciplinary matters as well as his attitude regarding overstepping of the police functions and the issue of use of force. It -- particularly because it relates to allegations of police misconduct and the improper use of force during the time-period that is relevant to this case. Secondly, Your Honour, this is a document that was obviously drafted and signed and prepared by Mr. Boskoski himself. It was a document that has been on the 65 ter list for quite some time. It had been disclosed to the Defence, I believe, from the start of this case. The Defence could have used it if they wished to cross-examine witnesses; they did not but that's their choice. But given those factors, and given the fact -- particularly in light of the fact that it was Mr. Boskoski himself who produced the document, I would submit there is absolutely no prejudice to the Defence in admitting it at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document will be received by the Chamber. The relevance to issues in this case is self-evident, and the fact that it is, on its face, a document of accused Mr. Boskoski himself, in the view of the Chamber, not only commends its admission but indicates that there cannot be any material prejudice of the type submitted by Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be received as Exhibit P531, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I believe we've reached a convenient time, Ms. Issa, for the first break. We will adjourn now and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I turn to the next exhibit, Your Honour, I would just ask that exhibit that has been marked P526 to be please marked under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like to turn your attention to tab 21 of the binder, 65 ter 412, Mr. Kuehnel. Do you see that first page, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it's from the Republic of Macedonia, the government of the Republic of Macedonia, dated 12 November 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that, that's correct, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it's addressed to the Ministry of the Interior regarding our letter number 24-95/1, dated 8 March 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can please turn to page 2. Just to draw your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to the title on that document. It's titled as a draft resolution, condemning instances of use of force by members of the Ministry of the Interior and promoting the realisation of the guaranteed basic freedoms and rights of the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia and it's dated February 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we could please go to page 4. Just to draw your attention, Mr. Kuehnel. It refers -- the document refers to under the heading of resolution, resolution to condemn the occurrence by the use of force by the members of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and to promote the execution of guaranteed fundamental freedoms and rights of the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And finally, if we can please go to the last page, and we see the signature line which says Stojan Andov, by hand, president of the assembly of the Republic of Macedonia. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, do you know where this document came from?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We got it as a reply to our RFAs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honours I'd like to tender this as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we don't object to the admission of the document but as previously with regard to one of the disciplinary document, we'd wish to indicate that the resolution or the suggestion resolution, in any case, relate to events that took place prior to the month of March 2001; that is, prior to the time when Mr. Boskoski became the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P532, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Turning, then, to tab 22. The 65 ter number's 1075.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, do you see that document on your screen?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it. That's the same one as I saw in the -- in Ministry of Interior in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where did you obtain it from?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got it from the archive of the human resources unit in the sector for communal affairs, and I asked for that file.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can please draw your attention to page 3 of that document. Just to draw your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to the document which is dated 27 June 2001 at the top. And underneath the heading decision it reads as follows: "Tarculovski, Mladen Johan with the workplace inspector associate in the directory for security of persons and objects at the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia is redeployed to the workplace inspector associate for security of the president of the RM in the department for security of the president of the RM, sector for security at the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia, starting from 1 July 2001."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I see that Mr. Apostolski is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the transcript I see that we have a document of the 27th of July 2001, while on e-court we are seeing a document of 20th of December of 2000. Is this the document in question?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Actually, we should be looking at the next page, and I thank Mr. Apostolski for drawing that to my attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we look at the next paragraph, Mr. Kuehnel, it states the following: "The workplace to which the named person is redeployed has the status of a workplace with special duties and authorisations according to the law of the interior." And then continues at paragraph 3 and it states: "To accomplish the work and the tasks at the workplace in which he is redeployed, the named person has the right to a salary, for a full working time as an average value of the workplace in the amount of 600 points." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can draw your attention to the very last paragraph in that-- on that page, it states the following: "The redeployment is made so that the conduct of the function of the ministry will be more efficient and especially if that means improvement of the organisation of the work in the frame of the organisational unit which is the same or similar in the nature of the sphere of action and with the knowledge and work capability" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters don't have the text.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If I can just pick up then from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you will need to read more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I know I have been warned. Thank you. "And if, with the knowledge and work compatibility, better results are going to be accomplished by working in a different workplace." And if I can please ask Madam Registrar to turn to the next page, page 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just drawing your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to the screen on the right-hand side, there's the seal, stamp of the Ministry of Interior, and it's signed by minister of the interior, Ljube Boskoski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I'd like to tender this as the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P533, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to tab 23, 65 ter 1050. Sorry, actually, I misspoke. If we can please go to tab 25, which is an exhibit that has already been admitted as P00368.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, do you recognise the photo display that is in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it. It's an annex to an interview that I conducted with Mr. Majovic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And just so that it's clear for the record, the person you referred to was Mario Jurisic?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] It was an interview with Mario Jurisic, that's correct, Frau Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. And there's a circle around photo number 9. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is a photo of Mr. Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Where does -- do you know where that photo comes from?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know where it comes from. We made an RFA request to the ministry in Macedonia, to the government - I'm correcting myself - and as a reply to the RFA, we received these photographs, among other things.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And can you briefly explain how the photo board was compiled.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photo board was compiled by the Map and Visual Unit of the Tribunal, because we asked them to do so. And this particular board is one of several boards. It shows the same number of pictures and for the purposes of such a board we asked them to produce these photographs for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And regarding this particular photo board, do you recognise the handwriting on it?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can please ask Madam Registrar to please scroll down to the bottom.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see two different types of handwriting on this photo board. One is on the upper end, that's my own handwriting; and at the bottom it is the handwriting of Mr. Mario Jurisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you mentioned that the board was compiled by the Mapping Unit. Did you provide the unit with any particular instructions in compiling this photo board?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did give them instructions. I told the Photo Unit that we were going to need photographs, a photo board, which, among other things, would also contain the photograph of Johan Tarculovski. I also gave instructions which said that the other person showing should have the same biometric data more or less and there should be no major deviations from the person that is to be compared. I also gave them the instructions, there should be several versions of this photo board be produced so that the person that is supposed to be compared, the person shown under number 9, the photograph of Johan Tarculovski, that it should be put in different positions on the various versions of the photo board, the reasons being that we submitted this photo board to several individuals and we wanted to exclude a false identification because of the position of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Just for the sake of completeness, Mr. Kuehnel, you mentioned a moment ago that you recognised the handwriting of Mr. Jurisic and I believe you said yourself. Is there any other handwriting on that photo board that you recognise?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa. I can also see the circle around the photograph of Johan Tarculovski. This circle was made by the witness Jurisic himself when I was present. So it is a Mr. Jurisic handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think there's -- Mr. Apostolski is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since the witness just a bit earlier mentioned that he saw the handwriting of Mario Jurisic and his encircling the person under number 9, for the purpose of completeness of this transcript, can the witness be asked what was the purpose of the circle, the comment as to why the circle was made.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, when you showed Mr. Jurisic the photo board, what did you say to him?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information and questions I made are documented in the transcript of the interview as a standard -- a standard procedure, and the circle which was put around number 9 is a result of the presentation of this photo board and shows the identification of that person. That was the reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you -- when you showed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Tarculovski -- that fellow again, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. And there may have been a mistake in interpretation. My comment was on the remarks on the bottom, the remarks made by Mr. Jurisic which pertain to the person circled therein.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The handwritten comments.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, do you know why Mr. Jurisic made the handwritten comments on the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Apostolski is on his feet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honours, for interrupting. My question is decisively what has Mario Jurisic written as comments on the bottom of the page regarding the circle?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can, Your Honour. But for fairness and for the purpose of the transcript, I would like the witness to point this out, since he said that -- the witness said that Mario Jurisic circled number 9, and we would like to see what his comments are on this person circled under the number 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, if you're able to accommodate Mr. Apostolski, please do so; otherwise, it can be dealt with in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, it can be. And just to save time, Your Honours, I refer the Chamber to pages 3306 to 3307 to Mario Jurisic's testimony where he related what the comments were on the -- as to this -- on the photo board that he wrote.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Moving, then, on to tab 26, Exhibit number P00436. Actually, before I -- before I move on to that exhibit I would just like to clarify one matter, if I could.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, you mentioned yesterday that you did not see any disciplinary records that related to events that occurred in Ljuboten in August of 2001 during the course of your search at the archives. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you see any cases recorded in 2001 or 2002 of any member of the Ministry of Interior who has been investigated for any misconduct relating to events that occurred at the Skopje hospital, the police stations, or -- or the court-house regarding any type of mistreatment against certain persons. Has anyone ever been disciplined for that, in that period, as far as you could tell from the records?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't find any documents in relation to this. That is quite true. No, I didn't find any information on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you find any records that related to any sort of mistreatment or cruel treatment that took place at check-points?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I'm aware. I didn't find anything. And I'm referring here to check-points in Ljuboten during the -- in the period of the events in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And anything specifically in different police stations in and around Skopje? Any mistreatment -- any disciplinary records relating to mistreatment of individuals in different police stations in and around Skopje?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came across cases of mistreatment at police stations, but they did not refer specifically to the events in Ljuboten. They were different cases not related to the people in question nor to the time-period.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can then go to P00436, tab 26 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, do you see the document that's on the screen, both in the English and Macedonian versions?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see both versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And this, for the record, is the list of weapons received by employees of Kometa dated 25 and 26th July 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. The document on the screen in the original is an appendix to material I collected and this is all part of an answer that we got in response to an RFA sent to the government of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if we can please turn to page 3 of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we do we would simply like to indicate for the record that a suggestion was made in the question of my colleague that this was, and I quote, "the list of weapon received by employees of Kometa dated 25, 26th of July 2001." In our submission, this fact should be established first and the evidence, as we see it, has not been established on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. There's substance in that, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I was thinking of the testimony of Mr. Miodrag Stojanovski who testified to these facts, but I don't necessarily have to refer to it in that title in that form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that might be better, as this is a factual matter of some dispute.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, Your Honour, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply in fairness to my colleague, Your Honour, the Prosecutor is quite correct that Mr. Miodrag Stojanovski gave evidence on that point. However, he did not suggest that all of them. He indicated that in his belief, a number of them might have been. And he also indicated, as far as we recall, that he did not verify that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'll just carry on then, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, if I can draw your attention to page 3 at column marked number 15?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And perhaps we can just try and enlarge that, if we could, on the e-court screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you see that column marked number 15. It refers to a name, first name Robert, and next to it is illegible. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I can then turn to page 7 in that document. And just to draw your attention next to the number 40, you see a name there that is -- that refers to a Zoran Markovski. Do you see that? ?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention to the very last name on that page which says Nikolovski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can please go to page 8. And the name Nikolovski continues on to the next page at the top of the column, the first name is Kire. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Then if we can please go to page 9. If I can draw your attention to the column marked number 54.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that name is Goce Ralevski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can then please go back to page 4. And I'd like to just turn -- draw your attention to column number 21, Zoran Jovanovski.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then right below that you see column 22, which is Vlado Janev?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then column 23 is Aleksander Janevski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, initially -- let me ask you this. Mr. Kuehnel, do you know a person named Robert Zlatanov?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know such a person.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And who is that person?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Robert Zlatanov is an employee of the security company Kometa, and I know of him because he is referred to in other documents too. And we conducted an interview with Robert Zlatanov. The name here in this list, under the number 15, you can see it in the Macedonian original, it's hard to read here --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... If we can please go back to page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you're referring to column 15. We see that in the English.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can please look at the Macedonian for a moment. Under column 15 --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, when Mr. Zlatanov was interviewed, was he asked whether or not he received weapons from PSOLO?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was asked. And he admitted it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can then just turn to tab 29, 65 ter number 29.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where did you obtain it?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received this document, too, as an answer to our request for assistance, the request for assistance we addressed to the government of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I can just refer you to the first paragraph in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I can Madam Registrar to enlarge that, please. If we can enlarge the first two paragraphs. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it says the following: "In connection to your letter under the above-mentioned number and date, we inform you that the association for trading and services, Kometa, DOOEL, export/import, Skopje was issued permission to work by the Ministry of Interior with the decision number 21-42811/1, dated 18 December 2000, for activities - securing persons and properties in way of offering services. At the same time, we inform you that the founder of this agency is Zoran Jovanovski, born on 22 January 1963, in Skopje, manager with no restrictions, registered in the Basic Court Skopje I. "In the procedure of issuing permission to work to this agency, it was necessary to provide five licences for conducting tasks of securing persons and properties. Because of this, the following licences were enclosed: Licence number 70, for the founder Zoran Jovanovski; licence number 64, for Zoran Markovski; licence number 65 for Robert Zlatanov; licence number 66 for Kiro Nikolovski; and licence number 63 for Goce Ralevski." And if we scroll down to the bottom, please. You see that it's signed by the assistant of the minister, Erol Salih. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage I would seek to tender 65 ter 29.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, before being in a position to decide whether we would object or not to the tendering of this document, we would like to get some clarification from the Prosecutor as to the stated purpose or relevance of that document to the charges. If the only matter which the Prosecution seeks to establish is that in November of 2003 the five mentioned individuals had obtained licences as part of the organisation Kometa, we would have no objection. This is, as far as we can tell, the only purpose which has been put forth at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the letter is dated November 2003 at the top. But if we look at the body of the letter which I just read out, it actually refers to permission to work by the Ministry of Interior with a decision dated 18 December 2000. And so it is relevant because it demonstrates that -- or it tends to prove that the Ministry of Interior had authorised Kometa persons to work for the Ministry of Interior and these were the -- some of the same persons who were ultimately issued weapons in PSOLO on 25, 26 July 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour in that case we will object on a name of basis. First the indication given by my colleague that the permission is a permission to work for the Ministry of Interior is quite inaccurate. It --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: By the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's by the ministry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So the indication is quite different than the one sought to be given by the Prosecution. Furthermore, Your Honour, the permission which was given at the time was given at the time in 2000 when Mr. Boskoski was obviously not yet a minister in the government. Furthermore, the conditions as we understand them under the law of Macedonia is that indeed a security agency such as this one must obtain an authorisation or permission to work as a security agency. There's no indication in that document or otherwise that at the time relevant to the charges the security agency Kometa was working for the ministry. This would be quite wrong to suggest that this document does that, in our submissions, and therefore, Your Honour, we reiterate our submission that this document is irrelevant to the facts as put forth by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document will be received. It is clear that the comment by Ms. Issa that the document referred to a permission to work for the ministry was a misreading of the document; it's by the ministry. But on the face of the document, that permission was one granted in December 2000 and not at the date of the letter, which was November 2003, and it related to -- for permission to work as a security agency or for the tasks that are identified in the second paragraph of the letter, and those matters, while not in themselves and on their own constituting final proof of any matter in issue in this case, are matters which go toward proof of some of those matters establishing, thereby sufficient relevance for admission. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P534, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, are you familiar with a person -- one of the persons that we just saw on that list named -- or the name that we just saw on that list, named Vlado Janev?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that name.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was Mr. Vlado Janev interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. He was interviewed. A colleague of mine interviewed him. A suspect interview was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to listen to the tape of that interview?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] I had an opportunity to listen to the tape a time ago. I recently listened to parts of the tape only and I referred also to the summary of the tape, the written summary of the interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I can then refer you to tab 31 in your binder. And that's not on the 65 ter list, Your Honour. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I see that Mr. Apostolski is on his feet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, about the question which my colleague from the Prosecution asked to be brought on behalf of the defendant, we requested that these notes of the investigator be translated into Macedonian according to Rule 66(A)(ii). We have not received the relevant translation. Furthermore, we object that this witness speak on behalf of another person who was heard by the Prosecution and if the Prosecution felt that it would be useful in this case, this person could have been put on the list and called in to give a statement under oath here where he would be speaking the truth and by which the Defence would have enabled to cross-examine him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply to join our friend of the Defence of Mr. Tarculovski on this point, we think it would be quite impermissible of the Prosecution to try to elicit evidence from another witness through this witness if the person in question who, as far as we can tell, was available and was not called, this is for the Prosecution to bear the consequences, if any, of those and we believe that this evidence should not be led through the investigator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all just to address Mr. Apostolski's reference to the translation, the tape-recording was provided to the Defence some time ago, I believe. I have a receipt that's dated 5 October 2004. So they do have that in the original Macedonian language as well as the English translation. And secondly, I have not had -- I had not even asked my question yet. I was not intending to go through the entirety of the -- of the transcript. I'm simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you're on fair notice, Ms. Issa, that you're running into troubled waters. Please sail ahead, and we'll see when you reach --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- them with your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I will. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, to your knowledge, did Mr. Janev provide another name or nickname that he goes by?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I know of two names, one is Kunta and one is Crni.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did he provide his date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, he did. He provided his date of birth and it was in the year 1965, August, and for the date I think it is 9th, but I have to refer to some of the documents. This was just by my knowledge. Yes, 9th of August, 1965. And this part I also heard on the tape.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did he say who was brother was?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he say that, and he said that his brother's name is Aleksander, acknowledged.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Aleksander Janevski?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's known as Aleksander Janevski, while his brother is called Vlado Janev.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And just to clarify that, we're talking about Vlado Janev, so his brother is Aleksander Janevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. If we can then turn to tab 32, which is 65 ter number 430.2.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters have difficulties hearing the Prosecutor, so if the microphone could be adjusted, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just drawing your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to this document.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it is titled criminal report with -- against an individual named Safet Senovik and if you look at paragraph 2 against an individual named Aleksander Janevski, father Pero, mother Ljiljana, born on June 7th, 1969, in Skopje, in the Republic of Macedonia, with the address of Boulevard Ilinden, number 118. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can please move to page 2 of that document. If we can scroll to the top. You see that paragraph 3 refers to another person named Vlado Janev, father Pero, mother Mirjana, born August 9th, 1965, in Veles, in the Republic of Macedonia and it states that he lives in Skopje, Boulevard Ilinden number 108. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then if we look at, just below that, that's marked as number 4, states that Zoran Jovanovski, father Todor, mother Todorka, born January 22nd, 1963, in Skopje, the Republic of Macedonia, and it has the address as Klenoec number 29-A, Skopje. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can please turn back to the first page. And if we can focus on the second paragraph. The crime in relation to which this criminal report refers to is reasonable grounds for suspicion that he committed the crime of violent behaviour. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can please go back to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just drawing your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to the first four lines under statement of reasons. And it says -- perhaps we can just focus on that. It says: "For the reported Semovik Janevski, Semovik Janevski, Janev and Jovanovski there exists reasonable grounds that working as a group they committed a criminal act, violent behaviour, provided and punishable under Article 209 ... " Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention finally to the last four lines of that paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Actually, if we can go to the last page. Sorry. It says: "From the aforementioned it can clearly be seen that there exists reasonable grounds for suspicion that the reported Semovik Safet, Janevski Aleksander, Janev Vlado, and Jovanovski Zoran, acting in a group committed one criminal act of violent behaviour provided and punishable under Article 209/2 of the Criminal Code of Macedonia.
