Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Where did you obtain this document, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a criminal report from the register of criminal records of the Ministry of the Interior, and based on a RFA that was directed to the government of Macedonia I went to the archives and had a look at the file. I think I can remember that the RFA number was 113, 113.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... And why did you obtain this particular document? What alerted you to these people?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were various reasons for that. First of all, the list of the 25th and 26th July, 2001, which should be in -- read in conjunction with the accompanying information that received at that time, on this list there are the names of Aleksander Janevski, Vlado Janev, and also Zoran Jovanovski, also known under the name of Bucuk. So they're all listed on there. The second reason is that due to interviews conducted with witnesses, there was the reason -- there was a suspicion that these persons participated in the events in Ljuboten. And the third reason, there are indications because of the link in data with telephone calls of Mr. Tarculovski, that these persons, with -- that there was a link with Mr. Tarculovski with these individuals when these acts were committed. So all in all, this was the reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: At this stage, Your Honour, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will speak on the top of my voice --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... microphone, but I think the interpreters are not able to hear me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The concern is that I have may have switched you off. If so, please understand it was unintentional. It is to do with the growing weight of my papers. If can you find a way of solving that problem for me, we will avoid turning you off, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I will make a brief attempt at least to save you three pages, Your Honour. But simply at this stage the only indication we would wish to receive from our colleague from the Prosecution, that is the only matter of relevance at this stage, is whether this particular criminal report or charges as they should be known ever led to a conviction, Your Honour, and whether the Prosecution has that information and whether Mr. Kuehnel could assist in relation to this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I join the objection by my colleague Mettraux. I also object to the relevance of the document, to the extent in which the data here are accurate and reliable. As with my previous objection to the previously shown and tendered criminal report, I wish to indicate that any person can submit a criminal report pursuant to the law on criminal procedure. There is no confirmation whether the Prosecutor's office has processed and accepted this criminal report. We have no confirmation whether the investigating judge has accepted this criminal report, we have no data whether the Prosecutor filed an indictment on the basis of this criminal report and, at the end, we have no information on the outcome of this criminal report, what was the verdict of the court, and at the end I wish to indicate that the criminal report does not comprise the time comprised by the indictment by the ICTY, so I see no relevance for this criminal report because it dates back to 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, Your Honour, I note that this is a document archived within the Ministry of Interior, and the evidence, in my submission, is relevant because it demonstrates that these same men who were issued weapons in PSOLO on the 25th and 26th of July were -- were issued weapons despite the fact that they had a criminal past, despite -- notwithstanding that we don't know whether or not at the end of the day there was a conviction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Isn't that a fairly critical point, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How does that help us? Because here all we have is a criminal report, which is the first step that may lead to an investigation, may eventually lead to a conviction, or it may lead to nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's true, Your Honour. But it also demonstrates that these are individuals who were associating together, which -- which is something that -- that is, in my submission, relevant to this case and they were associating in a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The objection to the receipt of this document will be sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. If we can turn, then, to 65 ter 475, which is at tab 33.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: This is a document from the Ministry of Interior which is dated 26th January 2001. And it states at the very top, the Ministry of Interior is referring this document to the public prosecutor's office in Skopje. And it states: "Pursuant to Article 141, paragraph 2, of the Law on Criminal procedure and Article 167 of the rules on the workings of the Ministry of Interior," there's a submission of criminal charges. And the criminal charges are against one Vladimir Popovski, and if we turn to the second page, we see that the criminal charges have also been brought against Zoran Jovanovski, father -- sorry, I'm just going to wait for the e-court. Father Todor and mother Todorka, born on 22nd January, 1963, in Skopje. With an address number apartment 29-A Klenoec Street and describes him as director of Kometa agency and the criminal charges are for an act of aiding and abetting under Article 24 of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Macedonia in connection with the criminal act of burglary. And if I can draw your attention to the second paragraph under statement of reasons, it refers to, states the following: "Namely on 15 January 2001, at approximately 0930 hours, Popovski Vladimir went to the Kometa agency and asked Jovanovski Zoran to help him enter the Krimer Komerc firm located at number 182-B Orce Nikolov street, property of Velkovski Dimce from Skopje so that he could take the machines as payment for a debt. They agreed that the second accused would provided 10 Kometa employees who were to meet with the first accused at approximately 1700 hours in the vicinity of the Chinese embassy and head towards the location and forcefully enter the Krimer firm." Do you see that.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where was this document obtained, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document comes from the archives too.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does it have the same problem as the last?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I would submit that it does not, Your Honour, simply because at this stage it is the Ministry of Interior itself that is referring the public prosecutor -- referring these criminal charges to the public prosecutor, indicating that it is of the belief at this stage that these are criminal charges that are warranted. In other words, there is a belief that this particular individual has a criminal past. And I would simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, the problem is simple, isn't it. You have got a report of a criminal offence. There's nothing presently before us to indicate how that finished up, whether it concluded in a conviction and punishment, whether it was proceeded with a toll or what. So a report gets us nowhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How does this demonstrate a criminal past; that's your wording.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, it demonstrates, Your Honour, at the minimum that there were people that were given weapons because they had some criminal association or, as this witness put it, they didn't look like someone who was a police officer or who deserved to wear a uniform and a weapon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document won't be received, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And we've reached the time for the second break. So we resume at five past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we can then turn to the next exhibit, which is at tab 34. It's been marked for identification as P00369. Actually, if we can please go to the cover page, the first page. And just to indicate for the record, Your Honour, that there are only selected portions of this exhibit that is contained in your binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, do you see the -- this exhibit on your screen?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it's referred to as outgoing -- well, the title says outgoing calls, the telephone number 070279417. Where did you get this document from, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got this document in response to request for assistance number 77, from the government of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you say from the government of Macedonia, are you referring to a specific arm of the government?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was sent to us from the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what information did you receive regarding this telephone that's identified on this document, 279417?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Document is proof of incoming and outgoing calls for the telephone number in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you receive any specific information as to who this number is subscribed to?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the documents that accompanied this, this telephone number had a relation to a person called Gjorgji Todorovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So the information you received was that this document -- this number was subscribed to a Gjorgji Todorovski. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did you follow up on that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got information on several occasions about this number and about the person most recently as a response to an RFA in 1992/1993 [as interpreted], and we learned that Todorovski, in 2003 had left the ministry in 2003, and recently we tried to find out from the ministry where -- tried to find out where Mr. Todorovski is at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did you receive any information in regards to that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No more extensive information; simply confirmation that Todorovski had left the ministry in 2003, and further questions would have to be submitted in writing. That was the last information we received.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did you interview anybody in this case as to who the number-- this number belonged to?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I took part in an interview; it was a suspect interview, Ljube Krstevski. He was an OVA [as interpreted] commander of Cair and he was interviewed on that occasion, and during the interview, Mr. Krstevski said that the number belonged to Johan Tarculovski, and he had talked to him using this number during the events in Ljuboten. The precise -- the exact text of this interview is on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can ask for P00231 - it's marked for identification - to be called up. It's at tab 38 in the hard copy binders, please. And if I can ask Madam Registrar to please go to page 4. And for the record, Your Honour, I believe this has been identified or marked for identification as the handwritten note or diary of witness M-084.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you see, Mr. Kuehnel, at the very top of that page the name Johan with a dash next to it and the number 070279417. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we please go back to P000369 which is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the purpose of this transcript, I wish to inform the Court that regarding this note which is mentioned in this document we see before us about Johan and the telephone number, two experts have looked into this and it has been noted that this was changed with a marker. The telephone number was changed which was previously marked. The number previously marked was changed with a magic marker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, just to -- just to follow up on what Mr. Apostolski said ... Just in relation to the expert report, the indication that I have as to its findings is that the inscription with that number Johan, 070279417 was examined and that on top of the examined page of the diary had been made with -- that inscription was made with a blue felt tip pen and added beneath it with a ball-point pen is the name Johan, 07027948 with a 1 and, brackets, 7 and the penultimate digits, 8 and 1, were written on top of the other, so it appears that there was one number that was corrected in that range of numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is an evidentiary matter that may need to be resolved at later.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, it may. And I don't intend on tendering it at this stage. Okay. If we can then please just go to page 3 of P00369. Sorry, Your Honour, I was just referring to my notes. If we can look at the column 3 at the page 3. And if we can please have that enlarged. I think we're looking at page 2 at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now I just want to draw your attention to that third column, Mr. Kuehnel, that refers to a Valentina Radulovic on 10 August. Can indicate -- do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think the name Valentina Radulovic is the name of the first wife of Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just to make it clear, the number on the far left-hand side, is that number 70279417, and this is a log that was indicated on the -- at the first page that relates to the outgoing calls of that number, and to the right of that is another telephone number with the date August 10, 2001 in the third column and a few columns -- or a few rows down is the name Valentina Radulovic. So that indicates that that number 70279417 was calling Valentina Radulovic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how do you know, Mr. Kuehnel, that Valentina Radulovic was Mr. Tarculovski's first wife?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's common knowledge for one thing. Valentina Radulovic is a very well-known person in Macedonia. She is a handball player, and apart from that, the name was also -- was also mentioned in statements as being the wife of Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you refer to statements, what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Witness statements, this OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can then turn to page 7 in this document. And if we can please scroll -- or enlarge the third column.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You see that, Mr. Kuehnel, in the third column that same number, 70279417 is once again calling Valentina Radulovic, and the date is August 11th, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then if we can please go to page 8. And if we can focus on the last line.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you see that the number 70279417 is, once again, on the 12th of August, 2001, calling Valentina Radulovic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, finally, if we go to page 9, the first line.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You see that the number 70279417 is, once again, calling Valentina Radulovic, on August 12th, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What do the records of these calls to Valentina Radulovic's number indicate to you, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The records that we have show me that there is a telephone link between the two numbers, between the number that we assume is to be -- is being used by Johan Tarculovski and Valentina Radulovic. In other words, that there was a telephone link between the two.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. And before I move into another set of calls, Your Honour, I'd just like to clarify for the record, regarding the reference Mr. Apostolski made as to the diary that was referred to earlier, for witness M-084, I would just like to clarify in looking at the expert report once again in relation to the handwriting, that according to the expert report originally, it was -- the name Johan and the telephone number which is 070279417 was written down with a ball-point pen and the last digit of that number was corrected with a ball-point pen and then someone wrote the same number over the ball-point pen, I just wanted to make that clear, with a different type of pen. And I also just want to indicate, Your Honours, for the record, that the expert report regarding this particular exhibit is the subject of a pending motion for the Chamber to -- to review at this point. I just wanted to clarify that for the record in case I earlier misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. But I do not appreciate what its point and relevance is at this stage. It's the sort of thing that if nothing else happens, it may be addressed in final submissions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I take your point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're getting very concerned about the progress, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I recognise that, Your Honour, and I believe there's a portion that I have which may take me perhaps 45 minutes more and then I should be -- that should complete the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. I make the observation now, so that counsel are aware that we are subject to some strict time-limits with German interpretation next week. And we must be entirely sure of concluding this witness by Thursday. That includes Thursday. And if all counsel would have that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can then please go back to page 4, now there are several calls -- if I can ask Madam Registrar to focus on the first part of that page.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: There's several calls recorded, starting at the sixth column, by that number 70279417 calling number 070243818, which, in this document, is referred to as the number -- or the person is identified as Ljube Krstevski and the date of the call is August 10th, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it appears there are four calls that were made on that date. Do you recognise that number 070243818, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it. It's the mobile telephone number of Ljube Krstevski, the OVR commander of Cair. And it is an official telephone number.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how is it that you recognise that number? How do you know that this is his number?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: For one thing, Mr. Krstevski recognised it as being as her own number and she said that she was using it [as interpreted], and also this number also comes up in replies to RFAs that we received as replies from the Ministry of the Interior in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can then please go to page 7 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Starting from the tenth column from the bottom, if we can please focus on that. There are entries of 279417 calling Ljube Krstevski on that same number of 24 -- listed as 24 -- 70243818, on the 11th of August, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now earlier, Mr. Kuehnel, you mentioned that the Office of the Prosecutor carried out an interview with Vlado Janev as one of the persons who received weapons from Kometa. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to page 6 of this document, starting at the 12th column from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you see the name Vlado Janev in a series of calls that took place on August 10th, 2001 from the number 70279417 to a telephone number 70520576. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you have any information, Mr. Kuehnel, as to whether this is the same Vlado Janev with the telephone 520576?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the same person that I saw in various other sources. I also recognise the address, Boulevard Illiden 108 and on the summary of the interview with Mr. Vlado Janev, I can also see that particular telephone number.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you're referring to that interview that was carried out by the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is precisely the interview I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, I'm -- I misspoke and I said that Vlado Janev was one of the persons who received weapons from Kometa at page 67, line 5 to 7 in the transcript, and I should have indicated that he was one of the persons that received weapons from PSOLO police station. If we can please go to page 8 in that same document. About the middle of page, the 17th column from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you see that same number, 70279417, that you believed to be used by Johan Tarculovski as calling Vlado Janev on 11 August 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can then please go to page 10, at the very bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you see a series of calls once again from the same number, 279417, that you believe to belong to Johan Tarculovski -- was used by Johan Tarculovski, as calling Vlado Janev on 12 August 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I note the time, and I have another area I was going move into, so I would suggest that it might be best to stop now, if it's convenient. But before I do that, I would like to make a couple of redactions in private session, subject to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: To be reconvened on Monday, the 19th day of November, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.
